question: Can a fixed classical grayscale tone/layout descriptor recover AO6 case Oracle value that global semantic similarity missed, without using chroma, target pixels, operator signatures, fitting or blending?

feature_model.feature: concatenated bounded luma quantiles, 4x4 means/stds and normalized gradient quantiles followed by L2 normalization

selector.rule: hard Top-1 cosine-nearest development descriptor; ties by source_id
selector.ood_threshold: development-only 10th percentile of leave-one-development-source-out nearest cosine similarity
selector.ood_fallback: fold global operator medoid from BM1

controls.strength_oracle: exact BM1 analytically bounded scalar-strength control
controls.case_oracle: exact BM1 post-hoc hard case upper bound
controls.semantic_negative: exact BM2 fixed DINOv2-S negative result

branches.pass: freeze the simple hard selector and require a genuinely fresh unchanged confirmation population before product consideration
branches.fail: close simple source-only case retrieval for this population; retain BM1 Oracle descriptively and AO6/global fallback operationally

claim_ceiling: group-held development evidence for classical grayscale tone/layout hard retrieval among deterministic AO6 Look Approximation cases; not film, stock, latent mode, calibration, authenticity, population preference, final-RGB ML or product promotion
